summary: The list surface only — no trigger, no anchor, no open state. Positioning it is the caller's job.
useWhen: rendering a list of actions or options as a surface you have already positioned
the rows need icons, a selected check, or two lines — more than a native <select> can hold

useInstead.when: you want a self-contained dropdown with a trigger and open state
useInstead.why: Menu is the surface alone; Popover owns the trigger, positioning, focus containment and Escape

useInstead.when: one value is picked from a modest list of plain text options
useInstead.why: the native picker brings keyboard handling, type-ahead and the mobile platform picker for free

useInstead.when: it is primary navigation rather than a dropdown

guarantees: no `role="menu"`, deliberately: a real ARIA menu owes the user roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation and typeahead, and claiming the role without them promises interactions that are not there
notes: Each MenuItem is a real <button>, so Tab reaches every row. That is honest, and it is not the same as arrow-key menu navigation.
The role arrives when the popover that owns it does.

antiPatterns.why: the keyboard behaviour that role promises is not implemented; an honest list is better for a screen-reader user than a lying menu

antiPatterns.dont: using Menu as a dropdown without positioning it
antiPatterns.why: it renders in flow — it has no anchor logic of its own
